text: Urban vegetation reduces land surface temperature in densely populated cities.
Impervious surfaces increase heat retention and contribute to urban heat islands.
Tree canopy coverage is associated with lower daytime temperatures.
Satellite imagery can measure land surface temperature using thermal infrared sensors.
Green roofs provide insulation and can reduce building energy consumption.
Higher NDVI values are associated with decreased land surface temperature.
Dense urban development and low vegetation coverage contribute to elevated temperatures.
Machine learning models can predict urban heat using satellite-derived environmental variables.
